summary: The memory tree is the part I'd actually borrow: instead of the usual context compaction, UniiChat merges neighboring one-line summaries into a binary tree in the background with a cheap model, so every call gets a 128 KB view where recent messages are verbatim and older ones fade into broader lines, and the agent can zoom back to any original without losing anything. It's about as local-first as an agent server gets—your history is JSON lines in ~/.unii, one `bun Server.ts` runs it, and every window (browser, terminal, a Mac it can drive) is just a view into the single thread the server owns, which is a useful inverse of the many-sessions routing I do in PenguPool. The per-file design-in-header-comments and the "it's vibe-coded, expect bugs" framing make it readable enough to fork, which I respect more than most agent frameworks that bury their architecture behind abstractions.
